items.text: In published reviews of adults with atrial fibrillation eligible for anticoagulation, which interventions (pharmacist-led review, practice feedback, prescribing prompts, decision aids, or combinations) increase appropriate anticoagulation, and what is known about their effects on stroke, major bleeding and informed choice?
items.population: Adults with atrial fibrillation eligible for anticoagulation, in primary care or in programmes that act on primary care lists
items.intervention: Interventions aimed at patients, prescribers or practices to increase appropriate anticoagulation
items.outcome: Proportion appropriately anticoagulated (primary), stroke, major bleeding, decisional conflict
items.time: Reviews published to the search date
items.setting: Reviews of studies in primary care and community programmes

finer: Feasible with 30 library hours and four analyst hours a week; interesting to the prevention committee; novel as an overview with overlap assessed; ethical with no participants; relevant because the board chooses in June 2027.
summary: One review-level question with prescribing as the primary outcome and patient outcomes alongside.
